title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: PEARL'S TRUNK
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Pearl Whitaker, a dental hygienist in Boise, Idaho.
For thirty years, Pearl has said open wide, and people have said nothing back.
Then her late Uncle Ray left her a dusty old trunk full of magic tricks.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: TOO OLD?
segments.quote: How old would you be if you didn't know how old you are?
segments.author: Satchel Paige
lines: Her son Danny signed her up for the library talent night, six weeks away.
Pearl said, Danny, I'm sixty-one. Magic is for young show-offs.
Inside the lid, Uncle Ray had taped a line from the pitcher Satchel Paige:
How old would you be if you didn't know how old you are?
Pearl thought about it. Maybe thirty-five. She opened the trunk.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: ONE COIN
segments.quote: Sometimes magic is just someone spending more time on something than anyone else might reasonably expect.
segments.author: Teller
lines: The first coin trick looked easy. The coin landed in her soup. Twice.
Uncle Ray's notebook had a line from Teller, the quiet half of Penn and Teller:
Sometimes magic is just someone spending more time on something than anyone else might reasonably expect.
So Pearl practiced one coin every lunch break for three weeks. The parking guard started clapping.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE BREAK ROOM
segments.quote: He has not learned the lesson of life who does not every day surmount a fear.
segments.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
lines: Alone, Pearl was great. In front of people, her hands shook.
Her boss had a line from the writer Emerson on the break room wall:
He has not learned the lesson of life who does not every day surmount a fear.
So every day, Pearl did one trick for one person. The mailman. The janitor. A very surprised plumber.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE WRONG CARD
segments.quote: If you're not prepared to be wrong, you'll never come up with anything original.
segments.author: Ken Robinson
lines: On talent night, her big card trick went wrong. Five of clubs. The man had picked a queen.
Her mind went blank. Then she remembered Ken Robinson, the British educator:
If you're not prepared to be wrong, you'll never come up with anything original.
So Pearl said, sir, that's the card you'd have picked if you flossed. The room roared. Then she found his queen in a dental floss box.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: MORE TRICKS
segments.quote: Ideas are like rabbits. You get a couple and learn how to handle them, and pretty soon you have a dozen.
segments.author: John Steinbeck
lines: Pearl lost to an eighty-year-old tap dancer. But she could not stop dreaming up tricks.
Danny laughed and read her a line from John Steinbeck, the novelist:
Ideas are like rabbits. You get a couple and learn how to handle them, and pretty soon you have a dozen.
By spring, Pearl had twelve tricks, all with toothbrushes.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE BIG CHAIR
segments.quote: Those who don't believe in magic will never find it.
segments.author: Roald Dahl
lines: One Monday, a huge truck driver sat in her chair, sweating. He hated dentists.
Pearl remembered the last line in Uncle Ray's notebook, from the writer Roald Dahl:
Those who don't believe in magic will never find it.
She pulled a quarter from his ear. He laughed, and opened wide. Now patients ask for the magic lady.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Forget your age. Practice. Face a fear. Be wrong. Keep creating. Believe.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Forget your age. Practice. Face a fear a day. Dare to be wrong. Keep the ideas coming. And believe.
I tried Pearl's coin trick once. My moustache ate the quarter.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
